name: Liberal Zionism
summary: Liberal Zionism holds that the Jewish people have a right to national self-determination in a state of their own, and that this state must be a liberal democracy with equal rights for all its citizens. Its adherents typically favour secularism, free-market principles and a negotiated two-state solution, and criticise the occupation and settlement expansion since 1967. They defend independent courts and a constitutional order against majoritarian or religious pressure.
scope: The mainstream liberal strand of Zionism: Brandeis's 1915 case for Zionism within American democracy, the General Zionists and Progressive Party of Weizmann and Pinchas Rosen, the 1948 Declaration of Independence, and contemporary organisations such as J Street, Peace Now, Reform Zionism (ARZA) and centrist Israeli liberal parties. It excludes Labor, Revisionist and religious Zionism. Economic and social questions are mostly inferred, so many answers are low confidence, and the market-liberal and social-liberal wings differ on them.

keyFigures.name: Louis Brandeis
keyFigures.role: American jurist whose 1915 essay presented Zionism as compatible with liberal democracy.

keyFigures.name: Chaim Weizmann
keyFigures.role: Leader of the liberal General Zionists, signatory of the Declaration and Israel's first president.

keyFigures.name: Pinchas Rosen
keyFigures.role: Leader of the Progressive Party and Israel's first Minister of Justice, who pressed for a constitution.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Liberal Zionists in the social-liberal Progressive and Meretz tradition accept a welfare state, and Israel already has a state-guaranteed health basket; this is inferred, not documented in the sources.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from the social-liberal wing (Progressives, Meretz Liberals) accepting wage floors, while the General Zionist wing was market-oriented, so support is mild.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The General Zionists, Shinui, Kadima and Yesh Atid all affirmed free-market principles, though the social-liberal Progressive strand tempered this.

public-ownership.rationale: The General Zionists opposed Labor's state-directed economy and liberal parties favour private enterprise and minimum government intervention.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Social-liberal and market-liberal strands pull in opposite directions and the sources document no stance on rates.

unions-good.rationale: Labor Zionism owned the union movement, whereas the General Zionists were its opponents; liberal Zionists as a family are split and the sources are silent.

property-fundamental.rationale: Market liberalism supports property rights but the Progressive social-liberal strand accepted limits; no source gives a defining view.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Free-market liberalism opposes heavy regulation while social liberals accept it; no documented position.

cut-welfare.rationale: Liberal Zionists accept a welfare state in general; the free-market General Zionist wing might trim it, but the dependency claim is not part of the ideology.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective ownership belongs to Labor Zionism and kibbutz socialism, not the liberal strand, which favoured private enterprise.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Liberal Zionists stress civil liberties yet accept Israel's acute security needs; the sources give no position.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Liberal parties in Israel have backed cannabis reform but the sources do not show a settled position for the ideology.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Free expression and anti-racism pull against each other and the sources do not document a position.

strong-leader.rationale: Liberal Zionists oppose what they see as democratic backsliding under Netanyahu and defend checks on the executive.

state-harmful.rationale: The movement is about building and sustaining a liberal democratic state, and the Declaration of Independence founds one with equal rights and law.

limit-guns.rationale: Israeli liberal Zionists give no documented line on gun control, and security culture is permissive on arms.

empower-police-military.rationale: Liberal Zionists back Israel's defence but also criticise the occupation and military overreach; no documented position on budgets.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed in any source; liberal individual-freedom arguments and feminist objections both exist.

decide-locally.rationale: Not a theme of the ideology; liberal Zionists favour a single constitutional democracy with a national parliament.

rehabilitation.rationale: Liberal human-rights outlook suggests support for rehabilitation, but no source documents it.

traditional-family.rationale: Liberal Zionists are secular-leaning and oppose religious control of family law, so they are unlikely to treat traditional structures as foundational; inferred.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Liberal Zionist groups such as Reform and Yesh Atid generally support LGBT equality and civil marriage, but sources document civil marriage rather than same-sex marriage.

abortion-legal.rationale: The secular liberal outlook favours legal access, which Israel already permits via committee; inferred.

more-religion-public.rationale: Liberal Zionists favour secularism and oppose religious coercion such as the Chief Rabbinate's marriage monopoly.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Liberal Zionists accept active equality for Arab citizens, though race-conscious remedies are not documented.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed by the ideology and liberals divide on it.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Cultural Zionism (Ahad Ha'am) and the revival of Hebrew are central to the tradition, and Brandeis stressed a Jewish life lived in its own home.

gradual-change.rationale: Liberal institutionalism and defence of the courts and constitutional order suggest gradualism; inferred.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The state is committed to open Jewish immigration, while liberals are less restrictive on others; positions on non-Jewish immigration are not documented.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Brandeis was a Wilsonian liberal internationalist and the Declaration pledges fidelity to the UN Charter, but strengthening the UN is not a stated aim.

free-trade.rationale: The General Zionists championed free trade and limited state intervention; Brandeis is not documented on it.

nation-first.rationale: Liberal internationalism leans towards cooperation, though Israeli security concerns temper it.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Liberal internationalism supports it in principle; not documented for liberal Zionism specifically.

open-borders.rationale: Liberal Zionism rests on keeping a Jewish majority and a state with its own immigration policy, so open borders conflict with it, though Derfner would open citizenship selectively.

limit-growth.rationale: Market liberal orientation implies growth-friendly views.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not a defining theme; no source documents a stance.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Start-up-nation optimism exists among Israeli liberals but is not part of the doctrine.

revolution-justified.rationale: A liberal constitutional tradition rejects revolution, although Zionist settlement against British policy is the movement's own history; inferred.

experts-over-public.rationale: Not addressed; liberal Zionists defend professional courts and institutions but also democracy.

central-planning.rationale: The General Zionists were a liberal party espousing a free market and private enterprise, and liberal Zionism pairs Zionism with free-market principles.

socialized-markets.rationale: Liberal Zionists accept markets without requiring worker or public ownership, so the condition is not their test.

tax-inheritance.rationale: No documented position; the market wing would oppose and social liberals might accept.

basic-income.rationale: Liberal Zionist parties do not advance it and the market wing prefers targeted support; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The General Zionists and successors favoured free trade over protection.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Opposed to state economic direction in the General Zionist and liberal tradition; inferred from their free-market stance.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Not a theme for this ideology.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Implied by the movement's endorsement of capitalism and free-market principles; abolishing money is never discussed.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Market liberalism in Israel accepts established monetary institutions; abolition is a fringe libertarian idea.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Liberal Zionists favour individual rights and market bargaining over state-recognised class bodies; inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: Liberal Zionism is committed to liberal democracy and the Declaration's equal political rights.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Never discussed; the Zionist state was founded as a republic and Weizmann became its first president.

democracy-best.rationale: Liberal Zionists insist the state be democratic as well as Jewish and defend democracy against backsliding.

direct-votes.rationale: Liberal Zionists defend representative institutions and constitutional limits; referendums on major laws are not documented.

workers-councils.rationale: The councils model comes from socialist traditions; liberal Zionists support parliamentary democracy.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not addressed; Zionism's own claim is national self-determination, but liberal Zionists reject a Palestinian right of return and one-state outcomes.

natural-rulers.rationale: Equality before the law and equal political rights regardless of birth are central to the liberal Zionist framework.

political-violence-never.rationale: Liberal Zionists accept defensive force and the Declaration's creation of the state came through war, though they condemn political violence generally.

war-builds-character.rationale: Liberal humanist outlook and a peace-seeking orientation (the Declaration's offer of peace) reject the glorification of war.

separate-church-state.rationale: Liberal Zionists favour secularism and oppose religious control of marriage, though Israel's Declaration also keeps a Jewish identity and some accept it.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Liberal Zionists favour secularism and reject excessive religious influence on law; Shinui was explicitly anti-clerical.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The state's role in defence and justice is central to Zionist statehood.

military-superiority.rationale: Security-minded liberal Zionists support Israel's qualitative military edge, although the general principle for any country is not documented.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Liberal Zionists want a state with a solid Jewish majority but equal citizenship for all; Derfner says the Jewish majority 'has to stay pretty solid', and the two-state case rests on preserving it.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The liberal and General Zionist tradition rejected Marxist class analysis, favouring middle-class and national frameworks.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Liberal Zionists stress equality of rights and opportunity; outcome equality is a socialist aim.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Liberal Zionists see Jews as a returning indigenous people and would not accept the logic against their own state; no direct source.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; liberal Zionists reject the settler-colonial framing of Israel so they would resist the general logic.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not part of the doctrine, which aims at a nation-state.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Capitalist individualism is shared but moral claims for self-interest are not documented.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Liberal Zionism is a rights-based liberalism with equal individual rights guaranteed by the Declaration.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: None of the sources link liberal Zionism to an environmental philosophy, so neutral is an honest placeholder.

limit-population.rationale: Zionism has promoted Jewish immigration and demographic majority, and no source supports active population limits.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Herzl's Altneuland and the movement's modernising aims reject anti-industrial views.

accelerate-technology.rationale: No source ties liberal Zionism to speeding up disruptive technological change, so adherents are not documented as taking a side.

human-enhancement.rationale: Enhancement is not discussed in liberal Zionist sources, and liberal individual-freedom and cautious views both exist.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Liberal accountability concerns suggest scepticism; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Liberal civil liberties argue for it while Israeli security thinking argues against, and no source settles the question.

restore-past-order.rationale: Liberal Zionism is a progressive modernising project aiming at a new society.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Pragmatism is common (Kadima, Yesh Atid) but not stated as a principle.

direct-action.rationale: Liberal Zionists work through elections, lobbying and courts, though mass protest was used against judicial reform.

means-match-ends.rationale: The ideology has no documented view on whether methods must prefigure ends, so no side is taken.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Implied by the modernising nation-building project; abandoning settled civilisation is never considered in the sources.

distribute-by-need.rationale: A socialist ideal rejected by market-oriented liberals.

production-for-use.rationale: Liberal Zionists favour a profit-based market economy.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The liberal and General Zionist tradition defended private enterprise and rejected Marxist exploitation theory.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Implied by the commitment to elected, representative government in the Declaration; class dictatorship is not discussed.

collective-farming.rationale: The kibbutz is a Labor Zionist institution; liberal Zionists did not require collective farming.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A Marxist claim contrary to liberal internationalist thinking.

taxation-theft.rationale: Liberal Zionists accept a state funded by taxation; this is a libertarian claim.

harm-principle.rationale: Consistent with liberal individual freedom but no source states the principle.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Brandeis argued liberalism failed by recognising only individual rights and not the equality of nationalities, so collective national rights matter to the tradition.

conscription.rationale: Israel's universal conscription is generally accepted by liberal Zionists, though they often object to ultra-Orthodox exemptions.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Liberal Zionists prize the vote and democratic voice, and emigration to escape is the diaspora condition Zionism sought to end.

positive-liberty.rationale: Social-liberal and market-liberal wings differ; no documented stance.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not part of the ideology, which favours a free press.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Inferred from liberal egalitarianism; Brandeis treats race as only one element of nationality, but no source addresses genetic ability.

organic-representation.rationale: Liberal Zionism favours party-based parliamentary democracy.

total-state.rationale: Implied by the Declaration's guarantees of freedom of religion, conscience, language, education and culture, which leave these areas outside state direction.

national-rebirth.rationale: Zionism is itself a national revival but liberal Zionists do not describe it as overcoming decadence; read literally, they are split.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Liberal Zionists accept the pre-1967 state and criticise settlement expansion and annexation.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Anachronistic for a modern democratic movement; authority in its state rests on elected institutions, not feudal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Implied by the equal social and political rights the Declaration promises all inhabitants; serf-like bound labor is never discussed.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Liberal rationalism inclines against it; inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: Liberal and Brandeisian universalism of justice and the Declaration's reference to prophets' vision of justice suggest agreement.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The Declaration proclaims a Jewish state in Eretz-Israel and liberal Zionists state that Jews need and are entitled to a nation-state.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The Declaration commits Israel to open Jewish immigration and the ingathering of exiles; liberal Zionists support the Law of Return in the Jewish case, with Derfner objecting only to Jews-only limits.

revive-national-language.rationale: Hebrew's revival is a defining achievement that Brandeis cited, and Ahad Ha'am wanted Hebrew as the main language.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Liberal Zionists favour private enterprise management; no documented position.

school-vouchers.rationale: Meretz Liberals backed school choice and market-liberal parties likely would too, but this is only a documented minority strand.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The General Zionist tradition opposed the budgetary policy of Labor governments; inferred for modern liberal fiscal conservatives.

economic-freedom.rationale: Free-market principles are central to liberal Zionist parties.

rule-by-example.rationale: Liberal Zionism relies on law and constitutional institutions.

national-self-determination.rationale: Brandeis argued peoples have a right to develop as nationalities and the Declaration claims it; liberal Zionists also grant Palestinians the same right to a state.

force-without-un.rationale: The Declaration pledges UN Charter fidelity but Israeli security doctrine accepts unilateral action; split.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Secular but not stated; Reform and religious liberal Zionists exist.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: No source documents whether liberal Zionists would limit welfare to citizens, and equal-rights principles pull the other way.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not documented; market and social wings differ.

class-collaboration.rationale: The liberal middle-class General Zionists opposed class struggle, but cooperation as partners is not stated.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Cultural Zionism values inherited culture and Hebrew revival.

dominated-front.rationale: Not part of the ideology, which is aligned with Western liberalism.

workers-nation.rationale: The class-based national organisation belongs to Labor Zionism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Declaration guarantees equal social and political rights regardless of sex.

ban-interest.rationale: Implied by the General Zionists' free-market, private-enterprise economics, which takes interest-bearing credit for granted.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Contrary to the Declaration's equality without distinction of race, and to liberal Zionist opposition to discrimination.

state-class-instrument.rationale: A Marxist claim at odds with liberal constitutionalism.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The Declaration guarantees freedom of culture and language, and liberal Zionists favour pluralism, though Hebrew integration is expected.

elite-replacement.rationale: Implied by liberal Zionist values; the sources do not discuss this conspiracy theory, which casts immigration as an elite plot.

proportional-representation.rationale: Israel uses PR and liberal Zionist parties operate within it without calling for change; Progressives sought a constitution.

national-mission.rationale: Liberal Zionists do not usually promote exporting their government form.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not documented; liberal feminists would agree, others are sceptical.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Liberal Zionists criticise the Netanyahu government, but not elites in general.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Implied by the liberal commitment to individual rights; eugenic restrictions on childbearing are not discussed in the sources.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Liberal Zionists criticise occupation abuses and want accountability, though this is not documented for past killings explicitly.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Social-liberal strands accept a welfare state; the General Zionists were more minimal but still accepted wider roles.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Implied by the Declaration's equality irrespective of race; the sources say nothing about marriage across racial lines.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Declaration promises equal social and political rights to all inhabitants regardless of religion, race or sex, and liberal Zionists stress equality before the law.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A socialist debate foreign to this tradition.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Liberal Zionists reject the settler-colonial label, seeing Jewish self-determination as a return of a people.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Liberal Zionists favour civil marriage and oppose religious control of family law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Freedom of religion and conscience is promised in the Declaration.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from liberal secularism, which would not write a religious slaughter ban into law.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Liberal secularists favour it but Israel has religious state schools and liberal Zionists are split; not documented.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Liberal democratic legitimacy through consent underlies the liberal Zionist demand for a democratic state.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist emphasis conflicts with free-trade liberalism.

population-transfer.rationale: Magnes and Buber criticised expulsions and the Declaration invites Arab inhabitants as equal citizens; Derfner stresses equality for Arab citizens.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: A libertarian absolutism; liberal Zionists accept state force and taxation.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Free-market support is shared but social Darwinist framing is not.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Israel's Basic Law bars parties that deny the state's democratic character, and liberal Zionists broadly accept this; not documented in sources.

separated-powers.rationale: Liberal Zionists oppose judicial overhaul as democratic backsliding and defend independent institutions; the Progressives pushed for a constitution.

vanguard-party.rationale: Implied by the commitment to liberal parliamentary democracy; Leninist party theory is not discussed in the sources.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Social-liberal strands accept; market strands less so.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Public housing sale is a British policy question never addressed by liberal Zionist sources.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The General Zionists were anti-Labor but no documented stance on strike law.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Derfner argues a stable Jewish majority is needed to avoid conflict between two nations in one state, but liberal Zionists treat civic diversity as acceptable.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Israel has lived under emergency law, but liberal Zionists emphasise rights and criticise erosion of democracy.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Inferred from the General Zionists' free-market, private-enterprise stance and their opposition to the government's budget policy during the shortages; price controls are not discussed directly.

party-controls-media.rationale: Implied by the liberal democratic commitments the sources describe; press freedom itself is not set out in the Declaration.

party-commands-army.rationale: Implied by liberal democracy's state-run, non-partisan army; the sources do not discuss party command of the military.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Israel gives Jews immediate citizenship under the Law of Return, and no source gives liberal Zionist views on waits for others.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: No source documents a view on legislator pay, and the market-liberal tradition does not call for such caps.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Liberal Zionist parties vary in discipline, and the sources document no principled stance on binding members.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Not addressed; Israel is not an EU member and liberal Zionists favour national self-determination.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Israel's president is ceremonial, as Weizmann's was, and liberal Zionists favour parliamentary government.

clerical-rule.rationale: Implied by liberal Zionist secularism and parties like the anti-clerical Shinui; rule by religious scholars is not discussed as such.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Implied by a patriotic, state-building nationalism; the Leninist defeatist doctrine is not discussed in the sources.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Implied by the Declaration's guarantee of freedom of culture and by liberal free-expression values; moral censorship of art is not discussed.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Liberals support limits on executive power; unlimited re-election is not stated.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall elections are not part of Israel's system or of documented liberal Zionist demands.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Liberal Zionists value the U.S. alliance and security cooperation.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Implied by the General Zionists' private-enterprise economics; banning rental housing is never discussed.

people-in-arms.rationale: A citizen militia has been part of Israeli history, but liberal Zionists accept the state army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Agrarian romanticism belongs to Labor Zionism (Gordon); the liberal strand favoured a middle-class urban economy.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The statement concerns divided states like Korea, which liberal Zionist sources never address.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Liberal Zionists do not hold this populist view.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Liberal pluralism suggests agreement, though not documented.

death-penalty.rationale: Israeli liberal parties generally oppose capital punishment; not documented in sources.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: A religious demand opposed by secular liberals.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Liberal freedom of expression suggests opposition.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The Law of Return is based on descent from Jews, but Derfner calls Jews-only immigration objectionable; liberal Zionists are split.

minority-language-support.rationale: The Declaration guarantees freedom of language and culture and liberal Zionists support equality for Arab citizens.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Freedom of religion matters, but the ultra-Orthodox draft exemption is opposed; split.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The Declaration called for a constituent assembly and constitution, and Pinchas Rosen's Progressives repeatedly pushed for a constitution.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Liberal Zionists place democracy and rights above this.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Liberal internationalism leans yes; not documented.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Israel's ambiguity policy is not a liberal Zionist doctrine.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Israel's head of state is elected by parliament, and liberal Zionists did not campaign against that.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Liberal Zionists and J Street favour a two-state solution; Derfner's Palestinian state would cover the West Bank, Gaza and East Jerusalem.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: This is a debate within Marxism that liberal Zionist sources do not address.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation is not discussed in the sources, and market and social liberal wings would differ.

collective-defense.rationale: Liberal Zionists value alliances, but the principle is not documented.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: J Street says annexation of the West Bank should be reversed and liberal Zionists criticise the occupation since 1967.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Not documented; secular liberals lean yes but Judaism's institutions differ.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The Israeli presidency is ceremonial, as with Weizmann.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Secession by regions is not a liberal Zionist issue, and liberal principles of consent and of order pull in opposite directions.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Special autonomous regions of the Hong Kong type are not discussed in liberal Zionist sources.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Implied by the secular, democratic state liberal Zionists want, headed by elected officials; a sacred ruler is not discussed.

character-from-environment.rationale: Nature versus nurture is not addressed by the ideology, though liberal universalism leans toward environment.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Implied by the liberal Zionist defence of the rule of law and judicial checks during the 2023 reform protests.

space-expansion.rationale: Space settlement is not part of the ideology, and no source gives a position.

leader-cult.rationale: Implied by liberal democratic values; public veneration of a leader as embodiment of the nation is not discussed in the sources.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody presumptions are not discussed in the sources, and liberal views on them are mixed.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist doctrine foreign to liberal Zionism.

land-redistribution.rationale: Zionist land purchase was voluntary, and market liberals oppose confiscation.

refugee-return.rationale: Liberal Zionists generally oppose a Palestinian right of return as threatening the Jewish majority, accepting at most a limited return for peace as Derfner does, though they favour it in principle for Jews.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Liberal Zionists accept two states along negotiated lines, but this is not stated.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Contrary to the Declaration's freedom of religion and conscience.

women-must-cover.rationale: Implied by the Declaration's equality irrespective of sex and its freedom of conscience; dress codes are not discussed.

common-currency.rationale: Israel is outside any currency union and the sources give no liberal Zionist view on shared currencies.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The Declaration guarantees cultural freedom, but the Bundist doctrine of diaspora autonomy was rejected by Zionists.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Brandeis argued emancipation failed to end prejudice, and Zionism holds that Jews need a state of their own, so fighting only for rights where they live is rejected as a full solution, though Brandeis allowed Jews to remain in the diaspora.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical materialism is Marxist and rejected by liberal Zionists.

no-bailouts.rationale: Free-market liberals dislike bailouts but the sources document no stance on them, and social liberals accept rescues.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Liberal Zionists opposed the 2023 judicial reform as democratic backsliding and want constitutional limits.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Not documented; liberals divide on quotas.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Free-trade liberals and social liberals would split on binding standards, and no source gives a position.

moral-incentives.rationale: A communist aim opposed by market liberals.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Implied by the commitment to democratic and diplomatic methods such as the two-state solution; revolutionary foquismo is not discussed.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Liberal equality implies it; Israel has no titles to abolish.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Liberal Zionists value Jewish history and Hebrew culture, but no source says how school history should be centred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Liberal Zionists reject colonial rule and Brandeis held that peoples have equal right to develop.

patriotic-education.rationale: Not documented; liberals divide on mandated patriotism.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Race-conscious admissions are an American debate that liberal Zionist sources do not address, and liberals split on it.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred from the Declaration's promise of equality and Derfner's call to end discrimination against Arab citizens; the sources do not address private discrimination as such.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Declaration promised a constitution and Pinchas Rosen's Progressives and Meretz Liberals pushed for one; liberal Zionists defend judicial protection of rights.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial borders are not a liberal Zionist concern, though Zionism itself relied on the Mandate and its legal instruments.

elective-rulers.rationale: Liberal Zionists support democratic selection of rulers.

minority-veto.rationale: Liberals defend minority rights but not individual vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Liberal Zionists joined civil disobedience against the judicial overhaul, which is a modern example.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred: liberal Zionists defend courts and the rule of law, with some natural-rights appeal in the Declaration of Independence, but are not committed to this natural-law claim.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred: not a defining issue; no stated position.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred: not addressed; liberal Zionists favour international institutions and Western alignment, but the idea of Jewish self-determination fits a plural world.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred: liberal Zionism is liberal and market-friendly, not Marxist, so a labour theory of value would not be held.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred: liberal Zionists are patriotic but not committed to a workers-first politics; adherents are split.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred: liberal Zionists are mostly centre-left liberals who defend civil and minority rights, not a workers-only left.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Liberal Zionism is committed to liberal democracy and rejects communist party rule.

missingStatements.text: Israel should give up control of the West Bank so that a Palestinian state can exist beside it.
missingStatements.rationale: Liberal Zionists and J Street treat a negotiated Palestinian state as necessary for Israel to remain both Jewish and democratic.

missingStatements.text: Settlement building in territory occupied in war should be stopped.
missingStatements.rationale: J Street opposes West Bank settlement expansion and liberal Zionists became critical of the occupation after 1967.
missingStatements.declined: Settlement building is a narrow single-issue position held by one audit; no-land-for-peace covers the territorial question.

missingStatements.text: A state may keep its demographic majority by controlling immigration, even if this limits who may settle there.
missingStatements.rationale: Derfner argues a stable Jewish majority is needed and so rejects a refugee right of return while opposing other discrimination.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow; ethnic-nation and reduce-immigration cover demographic/immigration questions better and the proposal is a single-audit view.

missingStatements.text: Boycotts aimed at a country to pressure its government are illegitimate.
missingStatements.rationale: J Street strongly opposes the BDS movement while criticising settlements.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow single-issue tactic held by one audit; not a defining position.

notes: Economic answers depend on the wing: the General Zionists and Shinui were market liberal, while the Progressives and Meretz Liberals were social liberal. Many Israeli and American liberal Zionists are increasingly divided over the Gaza war and the viability of two states, and some critics argue liberal Zionism is internally contradictory.
